newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Scitex sees improved operating results.
newsitem.headline: Scitex sees improved operating results.

text.p: Israel's Scitex Corp senior management said on Thursday they expect a continued operating improvement in coming quarters and a gradual winding down of restructuring costs.
On Wednesday Scitex reported a net loss of $0.17 a share in the first quarter of 1997, against a profit of $0.08 a year earlier. But in the fourth quarter of last year the company lost $0.57 a share.
Scitex trimmed its operating loss of $8.35 million in the first quarter from a $25.44 million loss in the fourth quarter.

"We view this as a positive first step in the right direction," Scitex president and chief executive Yoav Chelouche told Reuters in an interview that included chief financial officer Eyal Desheh and corporate vice president Erez Meltzer.
"Our plan does call for continued improvement on the operating side," Chelouche said. He declined to give any projections.
Once the flagship of Israel's high-tech sector, the maker of electronic pre-press, digital printing and digital video systems has seen its share price fall from $44 in 1992 to $7-3/4 now.
Last year Scitex rejected a buyout offer from Israeli-born entrepreneur Davidi Gilo to acquire the company for $25 a share, an offer that had caused the shares to shoot up to $21.
Noting that the stock is trading below book value of $11-1/2 a share, Desheh said investors should be patient.
"We believe the stock is undervalued. We will have to be judged by performance. Management believes in turning the company around," Desheh said.

In the fourth quarter of last year the company announced a restructuring that included sacking 400 employees from its graphic arts division and a reduction in operating expenses of $10 million per quarter.
Besides a decline in operating losses, the first quarter showed an improvement in gross margins and operating cash flow.

In 1995 Scitex had a negative cash flow of $70 million. In the first quarter of 1996 that fell to $7 million and in the first quarter of 1997 to $1 million. The 1997 figure includes a $6 million charge for restructuring expenses, expected to shrink a nominal amount by the fourth quarter.

The graphic arts group, where Scitex's electronic pre-press business is concentrated, reported first-quarter revenues of $112 million. Gross profit almost doubled from the fourth quarter while the operating loss was less than a quarter of what it was in the fourth quarter.
Chelouche said the results were achieved in spite of the fact that there was no improvement in the market, which continued to be highly competitive.
Scitex's digital printing group reported sales of $33 million in the first quarter. "We continue to believe it is a growing area of opportunity for us," Chelouche said.
"We are continuing to make significant investment in research and development."
The digital video division, which had revenues of $18 million for the first quarter, roughly broke even, he said.
